Photorealistic means footage that an ordinary viewer could plausibly mistake for a recording of real events. AI-written scripts, synthetic narration and obvious cartoons alone do not qualify.
The named technology is Sora or an open-source video-generation counterpart. Evidence identifying only an unspecified AI tool does not establish this element.
The surrounding discussion makes YouTube the main example, without expressly excluding comparable video platforms.

In short order means soon after the February 18, 2024 post. It supplies no defensible last calendar day. No numerical deadline is imposed, and examples nearly two years later cannot establish the near-term timing.
Using the named tools is part of the predicted practice, not a separate conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish that, shortly after the post, deceptive operators began publishing photorealistic fabricated videos made with Sora or an open-source counterpart for advertising income. The records must connect the videos, generation tool, deceptive presentation and commercial purpose.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that the specified practice did not begin within the near-term period meant by the claim. Missing examples in a search, or Sora's release date alone, cannot establish this. A deadline chosen by the evaluator cannot justify contradiction.
